summary: Auto-EQ's Adaptive tone layer is effectively fixed for real voices: its three voice-balance inputs saturate for 97-100% of speakers, so where it measures the voice cannot matter. Replacing the measurement with the saturated values failed its equivalence rule on noisy captures (max 0.68 dB), and against the clean-voice curve neither version was better, so the code stays and the curves are described as tone presets rather than voice-adapted.

findings.measurement_point: decided without a run: the measurement cannot change the intended curve

rule_8b.rule: fixed offsets within 0.1 dB of today's in >= 95% of cases and within 0.5 dB in all; status identical in >= 99%
rule_8b.note: all deviations were on noisy harness captures; every cross-take case matched exactly

rule_8c.rule: fixed offsets closer to the clean-voice curve: mean RMS lower with speaker-clustered 95% CI of the difference above 0, and worse by > 0.25 dB in <= 5% of cases

limitations: Saturation was measured on VoiceBank read speech; unusual voices or microphones may fall inside the range.
The intended curve is compared, not perceptual quality.
